_note: Timings you measured yourself. Leave a value null until you have actually timed it. The eval reports whatever is here and never invents a number.
method: One person (submitter), stopwatch. Review timings: 3 of 12 cases (CASE-02, CASE-03, CASE-05) via the Streamlit demo shell, timed from reading the panel to a genuine sign-off decision, not just glancing at the disposition line. Per-case raw seconds: baseline review [15, 17, 12] -> avg 14.7s; v4 review [73, 72, 72] -> avg 72.3s. The CASE-05 execution timed here happened to be correct (METER_BYPASS_SUSPECTED, matching ground truth) -- CASE-05 is known from results/run1 and run2 to be wrong on 2 of 3 real executions (see README's hot take), so this timing does not measure how long it takes a reviewer to catch that specific failure; it measures ordinary review time on a case of that complexity. Manual triage: 1 case (CASE-06, not previously seen by the timer, to avoid bias from already knowing the answer), worked directly from data/cases/CASE-06.json against config/policy.md with no AI assistance -- matching invoices to meter reads, checking the tariff rate, scanning payments, reading field notes -- stopped once willing to sign off on a disposition, action and adjustment figure. Took 4:41 (281s = 4.6833 min) and landed on UNBILLED_PERIOD, matching data/ground_truth.json. n=1; a single data point, not an average -- more cases would tighten this if time allows before the deadline.
